1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing (e.g., the recovery-code list and short instruction lines), though letter spacing is ordinary rather than notably generous.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense blocks appear in any instruction text; all guidance is short sentence-case lines, with uppercase limited to the codes themselves.

3.why: The screenshots are desktop-width with a centered single-column card, so mobile-size rendering cannot be confirmed, though the narrow layout suggests it would adapt.

4.why: Instructions are brief and plain ('Use an authenticator app to generate a code.'), but labels like 'Provisioning value' and the phrase 'protected one-way verification values' introduce jargon.

5.why: Only the recovery-code field shows an example format (placeholder 'ABCDE-23489'); the verification code and authenticator code fields are empty with no example shown.

6.why: The longest text block on any screen is two lines (e.g., the 'Shown once. Copy these codes now.' notice), so no long reading is required to proceed.

7.why: Secrets and codes are rendered as selectable text (manual setup secret field, provisioning value box, recovery-code list) so they can be copied, though no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code appears on the authenticator setup screen; only a manual secret and a plain-text otpauth:// provisioning value are offered, with the banner explicitly saying 'Add this value manually.'

9.why: Nothing in the screenshots confirms or denies autofill/password-manager support; there are no password fields and no visible autocomplete cues.

10.why: Each screen has a bold step heading and a prominent blue primary button, but some screens (MFA settings, recovery-code confirmation) show two buttons at once, slightly diluting the single primary action.

11.why: Most steps ask for one action, but the MFA settings page presents 'Regenerate recovery codes' and 'Log out' together, and the confirmation screen shows both 'Verify recovery code' and 'Generate replacement codes'.

12.why: Actions produce plain feedback such as 'Authenticator created. Add this value manually.', 'Recovery code confirmed.', and 'Authenticator MFA is active.', though sign-in gives no explicit 'code sent' statement (only a mock Logs note) and logout is confirmed only in the Logs panel.

13.why: The error message invites retry and recovery codes can be regenerated, but regeneration consumes an existing code, and no resend option for the verification code or reveal/hide control is shown.

14.why: The only observed error, 'Unable to complete this request. Please try again.', does not state the problem, though it is non-blaming and suggests retrying.

15.why: No countdowns or reading time limits appear on any screen, and the provisioning URI specifies period=120, giving a generous 120-second code-entry window.
